neighbours.label: a preposition that opens a stretch of time something must last through (during, throughout, through, on the hour), as against the same prepositions for places
fire: Deer need extra fat to make it through the long winter.
Hummingbirds feed heavily during the warm months.
Ferries depart on the half hour from the main pier.
The heater runs throughout the coldest weeks of the year.
Workers will close the lane during the bridge repairs.
Squirrels store acorns to get through the lean months.
A laptop uses little power over the course of a month.
Extra trains will run during the festival each August.
quiet: Deer need extra space to walk through the dense forest.
Hummingbirds feed from flowers along the garden wall.
Ferries depart from the main pier beside the ticket office.
The heater sits against the back wall of the garage.
Workers will close the lane beside the bridge entrance.
Squirrels store acorns inside the hollow trunk of an oak.
A laptop sits on the desk over by the window.
Extra trains will stop at the festival grounds near Bristol.

notes: The peak tokens are prepositions, and they fire for seasons and schedules but not places ('throughout the room', 'on the shelf'). The − pole fires on 'school is out', so both poles concern calendar periods. 'Prices rose during the war' stayed low, so one-off events may not count.
